plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks carry huge golden faces that follow the sun across the sky. In early September, fields across the plains glow with rows of yellow petals around dark, seed-packed centers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Great Plains and farmland across North America, and sunflower fields in southern Europe
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not one flower but hundreds to thousands of tiny florets. They are arranged in spirals that follow Fibonacci numbers.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped lilac-pink blooms rise from bare soil with no leaves in sight. They carpet damp meadows as summer fades into autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Damp meadows and woodland edges across Europe, including Britain, Germany and France
plants.funFact: The plant sends up its leaves in spring and its flowers in autumn, which earned it the nickname 'naked ladies'. It contains colchicine, a toxic compound used in medicine.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Branches burst into fluffy, fragrant golden pom-poms. They brighten the Australian bush as winter turns to spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (roughly July to October) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southeastern and southern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem. National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring.
